title: A translated presentation retaining a strictly standard witness
statement: Let R and A be commutative rings with an R-algebra structure on A and A finitely presented over R [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Let pi in R have strictly standard image in A [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element], and let rho:A/(pi^4 A) -> R/(pi^4) be an R-algebra map. There exist n,m,c, a presentation P with n generators and m relations, c <= min(n,m), and coefficients b_I in A indexed by c-element subsets I of the n generators, such that rho(P.val_i mod pi^4)=0 for every i; pi equals the sum over I of b_I times the determinant of the matrix (partial_i P.relation_j evaluated at P.val), with j<c and i in I in increasing order; and for every j>=c, P.sigma(pi) P.relation_j belongs to the ideal generated by the initial c relations plus the square of the full relation ideal. Polynomial rings and derivatives are as in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative].

source.place: Stacks Project, Tag 07CR (lemma-desingularize), proof: choice of presentation through the identity for u pi, before use of Tag 07DQ

proof.text: Unpack strict standardness into a presentation, an integer c, its minor coefficients and the ideal-square containment.

Lift each quotient-section value of a generator to r_i in R using Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective. Substituting X_i+C(r_i) and X_i-C(r_i) gives mutually inverse algebra homomorphisms, by extensionality on variables.

Construct Q with values P.val_i-r_i, relations tau(P.relation_j), and lift tau composed with P.sigma. Evaluation after tau agrees with the old evaluation. Ideal.map_span and membership in the image under the automorphism show the new relations span the new kernel. The constructed lift is a right inverse. Applying rho to the new values gives zero.
Polynomial induction with the Leibniz rule proves pderiv_i(tau(f))=tau(pderiv_i(f)). Evaluation after tau therefore preserves all Jacobian entries, and hence the witnessed determinant sum.
Map the original ideal-square containment by tau. Ideal.map_sup, Ideal.map_pow and Ideal.map_span identify its image with the required containment for Q, including its explicit polynomial lift.

theorem exists_popescu_translated_presentation_data
    (R : Type u) (A : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing A]
    [Algebra R A] [FinitePresentation R A] (π : R)
    (ρ : (A ⧸ Ideal.span {(algebraMap R A π) ^ 4}) →ₐ[R]
      (R ⧸ Ideal.span {π ^ 4}))
    (hstandard : IsStrictlyStandardElement (R := R) (algebraMap R A π)) :
    ∃ (n m c : ℕ) (P : Presentation R A (Fin n) (Fin m)) (hc : c ≤ min n m)
      (b : {I : Finset (Fin n) // I.card = c} → A),
      (∀ i, ρ (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (P.val i)) = 0) ∧
      algebraMap R A π = ∑ I : {I : Finset (Fin n) // I.card = c}, b I *
        Matrix.det (fun j i : Fin c =>
          aeval P.val (pderiv (I.val.orderEmbOfFin I.property i)
            (P.relation (Fin.castLE (le_trans hc (min_le_right n m)) j)))) ∧
      (∀ j : Fin m, c ≤ j.val →
        P.σ (algebraMap R A π) * P.relation j ∈
          Ideal.span {f | ∃ k : Fin m, k.val < c ∧ f = P.relation k} +
            (Ideal.span (Set.range P.relation)) ^ 2)
